cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have direct access to real‑time or historical cryptocurrency price data, so I can’t pull the exact average Bitcoin price for each business week in 2023. However, I can explain how you can obtain that information yourself and give you a quick example of what the data might look like. --- ## How to Get the Data | Step | What to Do | Where to Look | |------|------------|---------------| | 1 | **Choose a reliable data source** | • **CoinGecko** (free API)
• **CoinMarketCap** (requires API key)
• **CryptoCompare** (free tier)
• **Yahoo Finance** (CSV download) | | 2 | **Download daily closing prices for 2023** | • For CoinGecko: `https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/bitcoin/market_chart/range?vs_currency=usd&from=1672531200&to=1704067200` (Unix timestamps for Jan 1 2023 – Dec 31 2023)
• For Yahoo Finance: `https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v7/finance/download/BTC-USD?period1=1672531200&period2=1704067200&interval=1d&events=history` | | 3 | **Identify business‑week boundaries** | • Business weeks run Monday–Friday. For each week, find the last trading day (usually Friday, unless it’s a holiday). | | 4 | **Calculate the average price for each week** | • Sum the closing prices for the days in that week and divide by the number of days. | | 5 | **Compile the results** | • Create a table or CSV with columns: `Week Start`, `Week End`, `Average Price (USD)` | --- ## Example (Hypothetical Numbers) | Week | Monday | Tuesday | Wednesday | Thursday | Friday | Average Price (USD) | |------|--------|---------|-----------|----------|--------|---------------------| | 1 | 1 Jan 2023 | 2 Jan | 3 Jan | 4 Jan | 5 Jan | $27,500 | | 2 | 8 Jan | 9 Jan | 10 Jan | 11 Jan | 12 Jan | $28,200 | | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | | 52 | 24 Dec | 25 Dec | 26 Dec | 27 Dec | 28 Dec | $30,100 | *(These numbers are illustrative only; replace them with the actual values you compute.)* --- ## Quick Script (Python) If you’re comfortable with Python, here’s a minimal script that pulls data from CoinGecko and prints the weekly averages: ```python import requests import datetime import pandas as pd # 1. Get daily data from CoinGecko url = "https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/coins/bitcoin/market_chart/range" params = { "vs_currency": "usd", "from": 1672531200, # Jan 1 2023 "to": 1704067200, # Dec 31 2023 } resp = requests.get(url, params=params) data = resp.json()["prices"] # list of [timestamp, price] # 2. Convert to DataFrame df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=["timestamp", "price"]) df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["timestamp"], unit="ms").dt.date df = df.drop(columns="timestamp") # 3. Group by business week df["week_start"] = df["date"].apply(lambda d: d - datetime.timedelta(days=d.weekday())) # Monday weekly_avg = df.groupby("week_start")["price"].mean().reset_index() # 4. Print results print(weekly_avg.head()) ``` --- ### Bottom Line - **I can’t fetch the data directly**, but the steps above will let you retrieve the exact weekly averages for Bitcoin in 2023. - If you need help writing the script or interpreting the results, feel free to ask!
